text:
Maya: Heads-up — seeing a sustained tail-latency regression on continuous-batcher starting ~09:11 UTC after the runtime push. p95 jumped ~300ms. Investigating now, tagging @Sam @Diego :mag_right:
Sam: Which deploy changed what?
Maya: Kernel arbiter heuristic v2 (tie-break by occupancy) + admission growth tweak (max_microbatch removed). Deployed at 09:08.
Diego: Any KV cache metrics?
Maya: Quick snippets from observability:
```
metric: continuous-batcher.latency.p95 = 540ms (baseline 220ms)
config: kernel_selector=arbiter_v2
microbatch.median = 12 (was 4)
kvcache.hit_rate = 0.42 -> 0.12 after deploy
nodepool: gpu-prod-3
logs: kernel_flip_count=136/min
```
Sam: kvcache hit rate tanking + kernel flips high — that smells like cache key layout / placement change when kernel variant toggles. If microbatches grow, more different prefix KVs get accessed per request too.
Aisha: CI-Bot reported compile spikes around the same time.
CI-Bot: Observability alert: container_compile_invocations on gpu-prod-3 increased x8 at 09:11 UTC.
Diego: Can you capture a pprof or perf flame? I want to see if the kernel path is thrashing between two implementations.
Maya: Uploading flame snippet from perf-top (trimmed):
```
flame: 40% kernel_selector::choose_arbiter
       25% sm_optimized_v2
       20% sm_fallback_ref
       10% kvcache::lookup
note: many short-lived sm_optimized_v2 invocations with warmup compile overhead
```
Sam: If arbiter_v2 is oscillating between sm_optimized_v2 and sm_fallback_ref per microbatch, we pay compile/runtime switch overhead and destroy KV cache locality.
Diego: Repro plan: run a replay with seq_len=256 workload and the new selector locally, instrument kernel_flip_count and kvcache keys. I'll run it now on a small pool.
Maya: Also saw admission jitter logs where microbatch size bumped rapidly:
```
[09:10:45] admission: size 4 -> 8 -> 12 -> 4
[09:10:50] admission: size 4 -> 10 -> 12
```
Sam: That oscillation is likely because arbiter_v2 sometimes reports slightly better expected occupancy for a different kernel, causing flips. Combined with no max_microbatch cap, it spirals.
Aisha: OK, proposed immediate mitigation: revert arbiter tie-break to stable_sort behavior and re-add microbatch ceiling (8) until we tune. Sam can you roll back?
Sam: On it. Rolling back arbiter_v2 to arbiter_v1 and reintroducing max_microbatch=8. Rolling at 09:24.
Maya: After rollback metrics: p95 dropped back to ~230ms by 09:30, kvcache.hit_rate recovered to ~0.40, kernel_flip_count <5/min.
Diego: Confirmed local repro shows the same pattern — arbiter_v2 causes rapid kernel flips when requests have mixed sequence lengths; KV keys touched per request increases and hit rate drops.
Sam: Root cause summary: tie-breaker in arbiter_v2 produced non-deterministic kernel selection across subsequent microbatches leading to frequent kernel flips, which caused runtime compile/transition overhead and scattered KV cache access patterns, amplifying tail latency. Lack of microbatch ceiling allowed uncontrolled growth that magnified the effect.
Maya: Action items:
- Diego: open PR to add deterministic tie-breaker and unit tests for kernel selection idempotency (assign to you)
- Sam: add deploy-time guard: alert if kernel_flips_per_min > 10 or kvcache.hit_rate drops > 25% within 15m
- Aisha: add e2e replay test exercising mixed seq_len patterns against kernel selector
- Maya: retro doc + blameless postmortem notes
Diego: Will draft kernel-selector PR today, include canary gate and revert plan.
Sam: Follow-up: add a quick metric to runtime: current_kernel_variant per worker to aid debugging.
Maya: Thanks everyone. We'll keep this thread for updates. :white_check_mark:
